messages.content: I want to settle the Boston flights before I authorize anything. Compare the complete combinations, not just the cheapest individual legs. I need enough margin for Tuesday registration, my spouse cannot leave SFO before 3:00 p.m. Friday, and I would prefer that we return together Sunday if the timing is sensible.

I found two workable structures. Combination A puts you on the Tuesday 8:10 a.m. United nonstop, arriving Boston at 4:43 p.m. Your spouse takes the Friday 4:45 p.m. United nonstop, arriving at 1:13 a.m. Saturday, and both of you take the Sunday 5:40 p.m. nonstop back to SFO. The current combined airfare is $973: $447 for you and $526 for your spouse. Combination B uses a Tuesday one-stop itinerary for you, the same Friday flight for your spouse, and separate Sunday returns. Its combined fare is $881.
Break down why B is $92 less and what we give up.

Your Tuesday one-stop fare is $374, saving $73, but it reaches BOS at 5:24 p.m. Registration closes at 6:00 p.m. Even with an on-time arrival, the airport-to-hotel transfer makes that impractical. The other $19 comes from putting your spouse on a 1:20 p.m. Sunday departure while you retain the 5:40 p.m. flight. That earlier departure removes most of Sunday together and requires separate airport trips unless you also leave early.
So the connection is not a real option. Is there another morning nonstop for me, including something other than United, that still protects registration?

Yes. Delta has an 8:35 a.m. nonstop arriving at 5:02 p.m. for $469 on your Tuesday-Sunday itinerary. JetBlue has a 7:15 a.m. nonstop arriving at 3:49 p.m. for $458, but its matching Sunday flight leaves at 3:05 p.m. Neither produces a lower complete shared-return combination than the United schedule. The United option gives you 77 minutes more arrival margin than Delta and keeps the later Sunday return.
Keep United in the set when it is comparable. I do not want it elevated just because of the name, but here its schedule appears to be doing useful work.

That is the right reading of this comparison. United is not the absolute lowest fare, but the $447 itinerary is the lowest option that combines a Tuesday nonstop with credible registration margin and the 5:40 p.m. shared Sunday return.
Now compare the Sunday choice on usable time. We plan to check out of The Verb, have brunch, and spend about two hours at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum before heading to the airport.

The 1:20 p.m. departure would require your spouse to leave the hotel around 10:30 a.m., so brunch and the museum would not both fit. For the 5:40 p.m. flight, you can check out, store bags, have brunch, visit the museum roughly 11:45 a.m. to 1:45 p.m., retrieve the bags, and leave for BOS around 2:40 p.m. That preserves the planned Sunday and provides about two hours at the airport.
What are the consequences of buying independently? I need my work ticket separate from my spouse's personal purchase, and I do not want one transaction to obscure reimbursement.

Buy two separate round trips. Your ticket should be Tuesday SFO-BOS and Sunday BOS-SFO for $447, with the Tuesday booking-page capture and the previously retained $409 Tuesday-Friday comparison attached to your expense file. Your spouse should buy Friday SFO-BOS and Sunday BOS-SFO for $526. Separate records keep reimbursement clean, but the airline will treat changes, cancellations, seating, and disruption handling independently. Matching flights do not guarantee that both reservations will be reprotected together.
Can the reservations be linked without combining payment or ownership? Also check whether these are basic economy fares.

Both quoted fares are standard economy, not basic economy. Each includes normal seat selection and one carry-on; checked-bag charges remain separate unless account or card benefits apply. After purchase, you can ask United to add a cross-reference note between the two confirmation numbers. That may help an agent see that you are traveling together, but it does not merge the tickets or create guaranteed joint reaccommodation.
Then select Combination A. State the exact independently bookable itineraries, total, and anything I should verify on the payment screens. Do not purchase yet.

Selected, not purchased: your United round trip departs SFO Tuesday, September 15 at 8:10 a.m., arrives BOS at 4:43 p.m., and returns Sunday, September 20 at 5:40 p.m., arriving SFO at 9:12 p.m.; current fare $447. Your spouse's separate United round trip departs SFO Friday at 4:45 p.m., arrives BOS Saturday at 1:13 a.m., and uses the same Sunday 5:40 p.m. return; current fare $526. Combined airfare is $973. Before payment, verify that both fares still show standard economy, confirm change and cancellation terms, inspect baggage charges, ensure the Sunday flight number is identical on both records, and preserve the $409 business-only comparison for reimbursement. After purchase, request cross-reference notes between the reservations.
